item.research_question: What are the creep deformation mechanisms and microstructural evolution characteristics of an equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy in the intermediate temperature range of 500–600 °C?
item.material_system: Equiatomic Co20Cr20Fe20Ni20Mn20 (atomic percentage) FCC-structured high-entropy alloy
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction melting with 99.9 mass% purity elements, re-melted five times, drop-cast, homogenized at 1100 °C for 24 h, cold-rolled 40%, and annealed at 900 °C for 1 h
item.test_conditions: Tensile creep tests at 500, 550, and 600 °C under applied stresses of 140–400 MPa; interrupted tests at steady-state stages cooled with liquid nitrogen
key_findings: Stress exponent ranges from 5 to 6 in the low-stress region (LSR) and 8.9–14 in the high-stress region (HSR).
Average activation energy is 268 kJ mol⁻¹ in LSR and 380 kJ mol⁻¹ in HSR.
Dynamic recrystallization occurs in HSR, refining average grain sizes to approximately 22 μm at 500 °C and 31 μm at 600 °C.
Dynamic precipitates identified as M23C6 carbides or Cr-rich σ phase form along grain boundaries in HSR.
Dislocation densities in HSR are distinctly higher than in LSR, showing tangled and curved configurations.
Stress-assisted dislocation climb controlled by lattice diffusion is the dominant mechanism in both regions despite high exponents in HSR.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that while stress-assisted dislocation climb controlled by lattice diffusion is the rate-controlling mechanism in both regions, the abnormally high stress exponents and activation energy in HSR are ascribed to the coordinative contributions of dynamic recrystallization and dynamic precipitation, where precipitates act as barriers increasing the activation energy.
item.limitations: It is difficult to precisely estimate the values of boundary obstacle stress and the decrease in the stress exponent due to the ambiguous interaction between dynamic precipitation and recrystallization.
quotes: The LSR was characterized by a stress exponent of 5 to 6 and an average activation energy of 268 kJ mol −1 , whereas the HSR showed much higher corresponding values of 8.9–14 and 380 kJ mol −1 .
Microstructural examinations on the deformed samples revealed remarkable dynamic recrystallization at higher stress levels.
The abnormally high stress exponents in HSR were ascribed to the coordinative contributions of dynamic recrystallization and dynamic precipitation.
